Hi Maya — thanks for the clear asks.

Short answers up front:
- Evidence rotation: we maintain log retention and exported artifacts for 90 days by default, with SOC 2-aligned snapshots available for 12 months on request (see control crosswalk).
- Pen-test cadence: We allow 1 vendor-initiated pen test per 12 months with a standard 2-week window; we provide a remediation summary within 30 days of completion.

I'm attaching a control crosswalk (SOC2_Control_Mapping.xlsx) and our proposed appendix language (MSA_Security_Appendix_v3.docx) with inline suggestions. Laura — can legal confirm whether the "12 months on request" phrasing is sufficient versus an explicit 12-month retention commitment? Karthik — please confirm the technical owners for each evidence artifact and whether 90d default + 12mo snapshot is operationally feasible.

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync Monday to walk through the redlines if that helps.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Maya / team — quick legal summary of redlines we propose: 

1) Evidence retention: change language from "12 months on request" to "12 months of archived audit artifacts, accessible for bona fide audit requests subject to a documented request process." This avoids an absolute guarantee while meeting audit needs.

2) Pen-test scope: keep 1 vendor-initiated test per 12 months, tighten window language to "testing window not to exceed 14 consecutive days, subject to operational constraints and prior notice." Add requirement for Redwood to provide a written remediation plan within 30 days and a closure summary within 90 days.

3) Audit rights: propose adding an explicit escalation path for evidence requests that exceed operational capabilities — i.e., Redwood will propose reasonable alternative evidence within 10 business days.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
